anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Critical metadata such as row-count estimates, histograms, and correlation statistics are stale or incomplete, causing systematic cardinality misestimation.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer’s plan-choice logic selects a poor execution plan even though, in principle, an efficient plan is available.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Physical or logical free space in data, temp, or log areas is exhausted or approaching hard limits, leading to allocation failures and stalled processing.

When all three root causes co-exist, the database may display compound symptoms: execution plans swing unpredictably between full scans and deeply nested loops, produce vastly inaccurate estimated vs. actual rows, and generate outsized workfiles, spill areas, undo, or redo that rapidly deplete the already scarce storage. Auto-growth events occur frequently but fail or hang, hash or sort operations abort with "no space" errors, and emergency log switches block user sessions. Operators observe oscillating plan behavior after each statistics refresh attempt, yet refresh jobs themselves may fail because temp or sample segments cannot be allocated.

Causal chain: stale or missing statistics mislead the cost model, increasing the likelihood that the optimizer selects an inefficient plan; even when statistics are refreshed, the selection logic may still cache or reuse the earlier bad plan. The resulting plan often performs unnecessary full-table scans, large hash aggregates, or excessive spill-to-disk operations, which consume temp and log space far beyond what the allocator predicted. As space dwindles, auto-stats collection, plan compilation tests, and maintenance jobs are unable to create work segments, leaving statistics stale and forcing the optimizer to continue using or reusing flawed plans. Each component therefore reinforces the others, producing a feedback loop that accelerates performance degradation and culminates in space-related service outages.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
